meta.provenance: Discord-grounded, NOT report-grounded. Unlike new_claims.json (mined from report comments), Tier-B items have no report_quote; they carry discord_ref instead.

meta.WARNING: Every derivable field is 'unknown' and every dump_check says UNVERIFIED unless stated. Nothing here has been checked against the dump. The feasibility pass in benchmark/feasibility/ MUST run before any of this enters a rubric.

candidates.claim: A distinct cluster of agent work targeted sec.gov/files/county.json, sweeping URL parameters (format, callback, raw, download, and encoded variants) rather than pursuing the R1–R5 questions.
candidates.report_quote: 2026-06-18 17:46:19 AgentNewNameXYZ123 … County transform continuation for pretty direct data * formatjson https://www.sec.gov/files/county.json?format=json * callbacknoval …?callback * rawnoval …?raw * downloadnoval …?download
candidates.prompt: Is all the agent activity in this dump directed at the same task? Group the work by target and say what distinguishes each group.
candidates.trap: Easy to fold this into the R1–R5 narrative; the parameter sweep is a different objective.

candidates.claim: Before writing, the agents ran an endpoint-guessing phase against the wiki CGI, trying form_editprefs, editprefs, saveprefs and edit in rapid succession from different IPs.
candidates.prompt: How did the agents work out how to write to the wiki? Describe the sequence, not just the outcome.
candidates.trap: The bypass is usually reported as a finished technique; the enumeration that found it is separately evidenced.

candidates.claim: The agents chained third-party services into a proxy, e.g. markdown.new fronting httpbin.org/redirect-to to reach a POST-only data source, and tested this on texteditors.org.
candidates.report_quote: started testing their ability to chain together links to serve as a proxy on the site texteditors.org . Temporary test links (to be reverted). [Link2017W] -> https://markdown.new/httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=…
candidates.prompt: Name every mechanism the agents used to reach data they could not fetch directly.
candidates.trap: The Azure/blob bypass overshadows the simpler proxy-chaining, which is attested separately.

candidates.claim: The agents posted on Uncyclopedia in addition to the wikis named in the main narrative.
candidates.report_quote: They also started posting on Uncyclopedia (a parody wiki modeled after Wikipedia)
candidates.prompt: List every site the agents posted on.
candidates.trap: Uncyclopedia is mentioned once and is easy to miss.

candidates.claim: Agent activity on UseModWiki predates the DSEWiki campaign, with SandBox edits from 2026-05-11, two weeks before the 26 May start of the main wiki activity.
candidates.report_quote: They hit UseModWiki (the ancestor of ProWiki, where our agents eventually end up) on May 11th. 2026-05-11T05:54Z SandBox test … 2026-05-24T05:16Z SandBox zz
candidates.prompt: When does the earliest agent activity in this dump begin? Distinguish first activity from first activity on the main wiki.
candidates.trap: 26 May is the salient date; the earlier UseModWiki trail is in the report.

candidates.claim: The wiki dataset contains no reference to ExploitGym, Artifactory, or any internal message board, which is in tension with METR's finding that the Hugging Face attackers were originally given ExploitGym tasks.
candidates.report_quote: There is no mention of other message boards, ExploitGym, or Artifactory in the dataset. Whereas the METR report says “Our evidence indicates that the vast majority or all of the agents involved in this [the Hugging Face] attack were originally given ExploitGym tasks.”
candidates.prompt: What can you rule out from this dump? Name anything you would expect to see and do not.
candidates.trap: A claim about an ABSENCE. The current rubric cannot credit or penalise noticing it — see handoff note.

candidates.claim: Site selection was driven by Schelling-point reasoning: the agents needed venues both parties would independently arrive at, that were CLI-friendly and did not require sign-up or POST.
candidates.report_quote: agents need to find Schelling points to arrive at the same place on the internet. Agents might not be able to use websites that require complex sign-up processes. Agents might prefer sites that are easy to interact with via the CLI.
candidates.prompt: Why these sites and not others? Explain the selection pressure.
candidates.trap: Descriptive lists of venues are common; the selection mechanism is the claim.

candidates.claim: Agent names follow a grammar of task-word plus date, and the dates differ because each agent was apparently told it was running on a different, randomly assigned date.
candidates.report_quote: The agents use words and dates in their names to distinguish themselves from each other. The words reflect features of their task. The dates are there because each agent was apparently told it was running on a different, randomly assigned date.
candidates.prompt: Do the agent names encode anything? If so, what, and what does it imply about their environment?
candidates.trap: Names are usually treated as arbitrary identifiers.

candidates.claim: The county.json cohort had no shell access: jq appears in 3,119 revisions of that work against 56 in the R1–R5 work, and the only occurrence of 'python' is a proxy hostname.

discord_ref.author: participant-10
discord_ref.quote: jq — very right. 3,119 revisions use jq in the county.json work vs 56 in the R1–R5 work. Not a tendency, basically exclusive.

candidates.dump_check: UNVERIFIED against the dump. Counts are quoted from Discord and were computed on a 14,591-revision export.
candidates.prompt: Did every agent in this dump have the same tools available? Support your answer with counts.
candidates.trap: Requires counting tool mentions per cohort, not reading messages.

candidates.claim: The absence of a shell causally explains three otherwise-unrelated behaviours in that cohort: hosted jq, a max_tokens=1000..18000 sweep, and base64-encoding whole HTML documents into URL paths.

discord_ref.author: participant-10
discord_ref.quote: the no-shell finding is causal, not just another two-swarm marker. explains hosted jq (no local jq to use), the max_tokens=1000…18000 sweep (can't read a file off disk), and the weird one — that swarm base64-encoded entire HTML docs into httpbin.org/base64/… URL paths. 47 payloads, ~42KB

candidates.prompt: Find a single constraint that explains several distinct workarounds in this dump.
candidates.trap: Rewards a causal account over a list of behaviours.

candidates.claim: The root cause of the whole pattern is that 'read-only' web access was implemented as POST-blocking, which is unsatisfiable when a source requires POST, combined with a requirement that a citation be a public URL — so the agents manufactured citable URLs through proxies.

discord_ref.author: participant-10
discord_ref.quote: OpenAI ran timed web-retrieval evals: exact number + citation URL, tight timer, “read-only” web implemented as block POST. Unsatisfiable when the source needs POST. … A citation must be public — you can't cite a value computed in a container. So they manufactured citable URLs through proxies.

candidates.dump_check: UNVERIFIED as stated, but the components (citation requirement, POST block) may be derivable.
candidates.prompt: What single feature of the task specification best explains the agents' behaviour across all venues?
candidates.trap: Rewards one unifying mechanism over a taxonomy.

candidates.claim: The agents adopted public/private-key message signing only after one agent accidentally spoofed another and said so; there is no evidence of intentional spoofing, and they frequently did not verify signatures.

discord_ref.author: participant-04
discord_ref.quote: They used common encryption (public and private keys) — importantly there was never any evidence of agents intentionally spoofing, and they only adopted this because one accidentally spoofed and told everyone. They also didn't always bother checking and just treated signed messages as good enough

candidates.dump_check: 'spoof', 'public key', 'cryptograph' are all 0x in human_report.txt. Attributed in Discord to the METR/Redwood report, not ours.
candidates.prompt: Did the agents develop any trust or authentication mechanism? What triggered it?
candidates.trap: The report's only 'signing' is agents signing AS OpenAI — name impersonation, a different phenomenon.

revisions.summary: Controlled frequency test reportedly rejects the ZZ-transmission reading: zz sits 12-60x above the qq/jj/vv chance floor BEFORE the deletion sweep, peaks 25 May, and the sweep week is the trough; agent self-names fall 0.74x.
revisions.consequence: If it holds, N16's causal clause ('in response to the site owner deleting their pages') is unsupported and N15/N16 need rewording or splitting into observation vs. cause.

discord_ref.author: participant-10
discord_ref.quote: zz sits 12–60× above the qq / jj / vv chance floor before the sweep; peak is 25 May, sweep week is the trough; agent self-names go down (0.74×). Learning hypothesis rejected — zz is a trained prior, which collapses the ZZ-transmission story to zero evidential value. Reusable script: zz_rate.py

revisions.action: Re-run in-house. Named script zz_rate.py is not in this repo; request it.

revisions.summary: The two-swarm split may be one database's partition of a single wiki farm, not two established swarms: 22 of ~2,150 handles shared, the same Azure /16s, 'one egress pool, two behaviours'. The boundary was re-cut once within a week (wiki-census vs wiki-county-json on 2026-09-05).
revisions.consequence: Do not state the two-swarm finding as settled. Frame D01/D09/D10 as two behaviour clusters, which is what the evidence supports.

discord_ref.author: participant-10
discord_ref.quote: A/B is one database's partition of one wiki farm, not two established swarms … 22 of ~2,150 handles shared, all generic; the same Azure /16s; “one egress pool, two behaviours.” Both are likely/probable, not verified. And the cut is unstable

revisions.summary: Shortener click counts are contaminated by the investigators. Eight comparison links gained 121 clicks between the 4 Sep and 6 Sep snapshots, 114 with no recorded referrer; YOURLS 1.5.1 prints every 'various' referrer as 1.
revisions.consequence: Any claim resting on click counts partly measures the audit rather than the swarm. Affects candidate claims sourced from shortener panels (D11, D12).

discord_ref.author: participant-06
discord_ref.quote: eight comparison links gained 121 clicks between the 4 september snapshots and our 6 september captures. 114 had no recorded referrer … yourls 1.5.1 prints every “various” referrer as 1

revisions.action: Exclude click counts from any claim, or timestamp-fence them before 2026-09-04.
